evidence.quote: Two questions of particular note are: 1. How do these substructures form? And, 2. How early do they form?

method.value: Image-plane model Fourier-transformed with GALARIO at observed baselines; up to 18 parameters

evidence.quote: we generate an image-plane model image, and use the `GALARIO` package (cite: Tazzari2018) to compute the Fourier transform of that image sampled at the same baselines as our observations.

key_parameters.value: Visibility weights multiplied by ~0.25 to match image RMS

evidence.quote: the weights provided by the ALMA pipeline need to be multiplied by a factor of $\sim0.25$ to match the RMS of the images

fitting.value: Bayesian nested sampling with dynesty, uniform priors; best fit = maximum posterior sample; uncertainties 95% inclusion interval

evidence.quote: Samples are drawn from uniform priors on all parameters, with limits listed in Table [\[table:analytic_priors\]]

validation.value: Bayes factors between model complexities; residual images and visibility profiles

evidence.quote: we provide a calculation of Bayes Factor in Table [\[table:analytic_best_fits\]] for each model considered, compared with the most complete model

findings_qualitative.value: Each disk is dominated by a single bright ring; five have a brightness asymmetry and four show inner point-source emission offset from the ring center.

evidence.quote: Each of the disks in our sample is dominated by a single bright ring.

claims.hypothesis: Substructures can form in very young, embedded protostellar disks
claims.experiment: Identified 7 VANDAM disks with rings/cavities/asymmetries and modeled with RT to get envelope masses
claims.result: Menv/Mdisk ranges 0.003 to 94; several sources ~1 or >>1
claims.finding: Substructures develop while disks are still embedded in substantial envelopes; these are the youngest disks with substructure known

evidence.quote: indicating that these features can develop while disks are still embedded in a substantial envelope of material and while they are quite young.

claims.hypothesis: The inner disks are centered on the rings
claims.experiment: Posterior of point-source position vs ring center in analytic fits
claims.result: Point source offset from ring center in all four sources
claims.finding: Inner disks are offset from ring centers

evidence.quote: none of the PDFs are consistent with the point source component being centered at the same location.

claims.hypothesis: The features are due to multiplicity
claims.result: No compelling evidence for multiplicity, but HST resolution is coarse

evidence.quote: We do not find any compelling evidence for multiplicity for any of the sources in our sample.

why_this_method.value: RT models give a more physical evolutionary status than spectral-index classes

evidence.quote: These are designed, in particular, to gain a better picture of the physical structure of these systems to better understand their evolutionary status

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Leaving the centroid free in RT fits was rejected since axisymmetric models could not reproduce asymmetries

evidence.quote: we found that the inability of our models to reproduce non-axisymmetric structure often affected the resulting best-fit model

limitations_admitted.value: HOPS-56B envelope mass is more uncertain due to nearby source subtraction

evidence.quote: the results for HOPS-56B should be considered more uncertain than the nominal errors show

limitations_admitted.value: HOPS-124 and HOPS-157 envelope masses may be lower limits

evidence.quote: the envelope masses measured here, and consequently their $M_{env}/M_{disk}$ ratios, might reasonably be considered lower limits

referee_caveats_inferred: Distance fixed at 400 pc for all sources
RT models axisymmetric, cannot fit asymmetries or offset inner disks
Visibility weight rescaling of 0.25 is ad hoc
Sample selected by eye, so no statistics on prevalence
Envelope mass degenerate with dust properties and opacity assumptions
